name: CA-26
label: Safe D

key_factors: Irwin's large fundraising and outside-support edge over Gallucci's thin cash
Prediction markets price a Democratic win at 95%
Open seat with no public polls adds uncertainty
model.rationale: The district's nine-point Democratic lean and Jacqui Irwin's decisive money advantage over Sam Gallucci, who holds only about $34,000 in cash, all point the same direction, and markets price a Democratic win at 95 percent. With no public polls or expert ratings, the forecast stays anchored to those fundamentals.
model.watch: A late surge of Republican outside spending or a sharply nationalized race could narrow the margin.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Julia Brownley (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
California's 26th District leans Democratic by nine points, and Julia Brownley's retirement leaves an open seat rather than a change in the district's fundamentals. Democrat Jacqui Irwin holds a clear financial edge, raising about $822,000 with roughly $366,000 in outside support, while Republican Sam Gallucci has raised about $377,000 and reports only about $34,000 in cash on hand.

Prediction markets price a Democratic win at about 95 percent. No public general-election polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the outlook rests on the district's lean, the fundraising gap, and market pricing. Those signals align in pointing to the seat staying in Democratic hands, with the open-seat dynamic and thin polling the main sources of uncertainty.
